claims.text: The kitchen states it uses no frozen foods, no retort/ready-made foods, and no chemical seasonings, preparing each dish carefully by hand.
A wheat-noodle ramen shop with shared cooking water and equipment; the menu and broths are not designed for gluten-free diners.
Broths and tare rely on soy-sauce seasoning, which typically contains wheat; the tsukemen is finished with a fish-based broth.
All broths are chicken-based, often with seafood accents, and toppings include pork chashu, so no dishes are vegan or vegetarian.

The cooking centers on South Indian and Sri Lankan legume-and-vegetable dishes (dal, rassam, vegetable curries) cooked from scratch with whole spices, so naturally plant-based and rice-based options are part of the regular menu rather than an afterthought.

name: 三笠観光会館 (Mikasa Kanko Kaikan)

claims.text: Menu is dominated by deep-fried and wheat-based dishes (tonkatsu, katsu curry, hamburg, udon) served in a shared high-volume kitchen; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Standard Japanese set meals and bento are served, which in Japan typically use wheat-based soy sauce; no wheat-free seasoning is indicated.

A Buddhist-vegetarian (shōjin) set is offered, but it is prepared in the same kitchen as meat and fish dishes and its dashi/seasoning ingredients are not disclosed, so vegan suitability and cross-contact cannot be confirmed.
A dedicated Buddhist-vegetarian (shōjin) set meal is available on the regular menu, giving plant-based diners a starting point to ask about.
Yogurt is served on the side of the curry so diners can adjust the spice level to taste.

Documented core ingredients of the yomogi mochi (glutinous rice, mugwort, red beans, kinako, sugar) are all plant-based and naturally wheat-free, making the signature item plausibly suitable for both vegan and wheat-avoiding diners if confirmed in person.

name: 奈良ホテル ティーラウンジ (Nara Hotel Tea Lounge)

claims.text: Cakes, the traditional apple pie, and sandwiches are all wheat-based and prepared in a shared kitchen, so cross-contamination with gluten should be assumed.
House-made cakes and the apple pie use dairy, eggs, and butter, and food is prepared in a shared kitchen, so animal-product cross-contact is likely for any non-vegan dishes.
The hotel indicates staff will discuss allergies and dietary restrictions with guests, while noting items are made in a shared kitchen where cross-contamination may occur.
Plain black teas, herbal infusions, and coffee are available, giving GF or vegan visitors safe beverage options even though the food menu is not suitable.

name: 寧楽菓子司 中西与三郎 (Nara Kashitsukasa Nakanishi Yosaburo)

claims.text: Several signature sweets are plant-based by tradition: warabi mochi (warabi/kuzu starch with house-made azuki paste) and Yoshino kuzu mochi are starch- and bean-based rather than wheat- or dairy-based.
